                    "fallbackMarkdown": "At ₹1.85 crore, Elite X is worth investigating, but I would **not pay a booking amount until you have a complete, written cost sheet and an independent legal review**\\. The advertised price alone isn't enough to decide whether it's a good deal.\n\nI checked the project's published RERA details and current online pricing information. Here is how I'd approach the purchase and negotiation.\n\n## 1\\. First, establish the actual total cost\n\nElite X is registered with UP-RERA under **UPRERAPRJ916631/02/2024**, with a declared completion date of **12 December 2028**\\. Its official website advertises starting prices of ₹2.10 crore, while another online listing advertises 3BHK units from ₹1.85 crore. That discrepancy makes it important to verify your exact unit, tower, floor, area and price in writing. citeturn237712search0turn237712search1turn237712search9\n\nHere is an illustrative budget for a ₹1.85 crore under-construction flat. These are planning estimates, not a verified quote for your unit.\n\n| Cost component | Approximate amount |\n|--------|--------|\n| Basic flat price | ₹1,85,00,000 |\n| Stamp duty, using 7% as a provisional estimate | ₹12,95,000 |\n| Registration and documentation | Confirm exact fee |\n| GST | Confirm taxable value and applicable rate |\n| Parking, PLC, club and other charges | Obtain itemised quote |\n| Maintenance deposit, IFMS and utility charges | Obtain itemised quote |\n| Interiors and moving costs | Depends on your plans |\n\nUnder the usual GST regime, an under-construction residential apartment that doesn't qualify as affordable housing generally attracts 5% GST, with the prescribed land-value deduction. Have the builder and your tax adviser confirm the actual calculation for this transaction.\n\n**The key issue\\:** ₹1.85 crore is already close to your ₹2 crore budget before additional charges. You may need a lower negotiated price to keep the entire purchase within budget.\n\n## 2\\. What to check before booking\n\nUse this checklist when speaking to the sales team. Don't rely on verbal assurances.\n\n### Booking due-diligence checklist\n\nof\n\n[Copy checklist]\n\nYou can verify the project using the official urlUP-RERA portalhttps://www.up-rera.in/\\. Registration is a useful safeguard, but it is not a guarantee that every approval, construction milestone or contractual obligation has been satisfied.\n\n## 3\\. How much should you negotiate?\n\nMy suggested negotiation strategy is to open below your target and negotiate the **total cost of acquisition**, not just the advertised base price.\n\nStarting price quoted to you\n\n# ₹1.85 crore\n\n---\n\nOpening offer\n\n## ₹1.68–1.70 Cr\n\nNegotiation target\n\n## ₹1.72–1.75 Cr\n\nThese are proposed negotiating positions, not verified market values or confirmed builder discounts. Your leverage depends on the exact unit, inventory, payment plan and competing offers.\n\nI'd start around ₹1.68–1.70 crore, provided you can justify the offer and are prepared to negotiate. Aim for ₹1.72–1.75 crore if the unit and terms are attractive. If the builder refuses, compare concessions before deciding whether to move closer to the asking price.\n\nNegotiate in this order\\:\n\n1. **Base price\\:** ask for a written revised offer on your exact unit.\n2. **Preferential location charges\\:** challenge any premium for floor, view or location that doesn't justify its cost.\n3. **Parking, club and other fees\\:** ask for waivers or reductions where the builder has discretion.\n4. **Payment plan\\:** compare construction-linked payments with any front-loaded schedule. Avoid paying far ahead of verified progress just to secure a discount.\n5. **Price protection\\:** ensure the agreement clearly states the price and which charges may change later.\n\nDon't expect statutory taxes or duties to be waived. A ₹5 lakh discount on the base price can be less valuable than a larger reduction in discretionary charges if the latter materially reduces your cash outlay.\n\n## 4\\. One issue I would investigate especially carefully\n\nElite X's declared possession date is in December 2028. Since you intend to live there with your family, you need to be comfortable with that timeline and the risk of delay. Ask for the latest construction report and compare it against the contractual schedule before committing. citeturn237712search0turn237712search3\n\nI'd also ask the builder for the exact carpet area. Online listings describe the project in terms of 1,800–1,860 sq ft layouts, but those figures should not be assumed to be carpet area. Get the RERA-filed area and your unit's agreement details in writing. citeturn237712search1turn237712search3turn237712search9\n\n## 5\\. Send me these three details\n\nI can help you assess whether ₹1.85 crore is reasonable and how hard to negotiate, but I need the specifics of the offer.\n\n1\\. Which 3BHK configuration?\n\n3BHK, approximately 1,800 sq ft\n\n3BHK, approximately 1,812 sq ft\n\n3BHK, approximately 1,860 sq ft\n\nDifferent size / not sure\n\n2\\. Which tower and floor?\n\n[Input placeholder: e\\.g\\. Tower B, 12th floor, east\\-facing] (Current value unavailable.)\n\n3\\. What payment plan did they offer?\n\nConstruction-linked\n\nDown payment / early payment plan\n\nNot sure yet\n\n[Assess my offer]\n\nMy advice for now: **don't pay a non-refundable booking amount until the exact unit, full price, refund conditions and legal documents have been checked.**",

                                "url": "https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/noida/strange-that-homebuyers-who-have-paid-in-full-cant-register-flats-because-of-govt-builder-dispute-hc/articleshow/134950768.cms",
                                "title": "Strange that homebuyers who have paid in full can't register flats because of govt-builder dispute: Allahabad high court",
                                "snippet": "The Allahabad High Court has expressed concern over the situation where fully paid homebuyers are unable to register their flats due to a dispute between the builder and government agencies. The issue was highlighted in a plea filed by residents of Ajnara Homes in Greater Noida West. The court found it \"strange\" that buyers who fulfilled their financial obligations are being penalized because the real estate developer has failed to clear its dues to government bodies. In response, the court has directed the state government, Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority, and the Uttar Pradesh Real Estate Regulatory Authority (UP-RERA) to provide a clear plan of action to address this issue. The case underscores the continuing problems faced by homebuyers in India due to regulatory and developer-related delays.",
